local_sub_summaries.local_summary_target: The patient lies on the left side with the left arm raised. Split-screen imaging begins with the probe on the left chest and a cardiac cross-section labelled parasternal short axis.
The probe is repositioned along the left chest, with directional arrows marking its movement. A rounded ventricular cross-section changes in size and visibility across the short-axis images.
A red circle highlights the ventricular cross-section while an inset heart diagram marks the scan plane. The highlighted cavity becomes smaller as the probe position changes.
The view transitions from a small ventricular cross-section to an apical four-chamber image. The inset scan-plane diagram changes orientation, and four elongated cardiac cavities become visible.
The apical four-chamber view is maintained with the probe on the left chest. An on-screen note introduces locating the point of maximal impulse as another method.
The apical four-chamber image continues, showing the septum and atrioventricular junctions. Labels identify the left ventricle and then the right ventricle.

block_summary_target: The patient is positioned on the left side with an arm raised. Split-screen imaging shows left-chest probe repositioning alongside parasternal short-axis cardiac images. A highlighted ventricular cross-section becomes smaller before the display transitions to an apical four-chamber view. The four-chamber image is maintained, an on-screen note mentions locating the point of maximal impulse, and ventricular labels appear.
global_summary_target: Left-lateral positioning and left-chest probe placement accompany a progression from parasternal short-axis images to an apical four-chamber view. Visual overlays mark probe movement, ventricular cross-sections and scan-plane orientation. The four-chamber view is sustained, with ventricular labels beginning to identify its anatomy.

local_sub_summaries.local_summary_target: On-screen labels identify both ventricles, both atria, the mitral valve and the tricuspid valve within the apical four-chamber image.
The labelled four-chamber image transitions to a modified view showing a structure marked CS. The display identifies this as an apical four-chamber view with the coronary sinus.
The coronary sinus remains labelled in the modified apical view before the image returns to a standard four-chamber configuration.
The view changes from apical four chamber to a labelled apical five-chamber plane, with an additional outflow region visible near the base of the left ventricle.
The apical five-chamber view is maintained, displaying the cardiac chambers and the additional outflow region while the probe remains on the left chest.
The labelled apical five-chamber view continues with the septum, atrioventricular junctions and outflow region visible.

block_summary_target: The apical four-chamber image is annotated with both ventricles, both atria and the mitral and tricuspid valves. The display then shows a modified four-chamber view with the coronary sinus labelled CS, returns to a four-chamber configuration, and transitions to an apical five-chamber plane with an additional outflow region. The probe remains on the left chest.
global_summary_target: The examination progresses from parasternal short-axis imaging to apical four-chamber acquisition in a left-lateral patient. The four chambers and atrioventricular valves are identified by on-screen labels. Subsequent probe adjustments demonstrate a modified view containing the labelled coronary sinus and an apical five-chamber plane with an additional outflow region. Split-screen footage links the cardiac images with left-chest probe placement.
